In detail

Sentrum is Oslo's city centre — not one of the 15 administrative bydeler, but mapped here as its own zone using the same official sources. Oslo kommune's own police-sourced Statistikkbanken data recorded 8,858 reported offences with their place of occurrence here in 2024, across a population of 1,528 residents — a rate of 579,712 offences per 100,000 residents, roughly 61.1× the citywide bydel average. This rate is calculated against registered residents, not footfall, so a busy central or nightlife/shopping-heavy bydel can read higher without that meaning it is unusually risky to walk through, and a quiet residential bydel can show a low rate simply by having few offences relative to its population. Sentrum is not one of Oslo's 15 administrative bydeler — it has only 1,528 registered residents (Statistics Norway, 2024), a tiny base for what is Oslo's densest concentration of hotels, shops, restaurants, nightlife and offices, with a daytime and evening population many times its resident count. Dividing a genuinely high absolute number of reported offences by that small resident base produces a per-100,000-residents rate far beyond anything a visitor actually experiences per visit — it reflects a statistical artefact of the tiny denominator, not a literal multiple of walking-around risk. Sentrum is still shown here, rather than left blank, because Oslo kommune's own crime table does track it as a real, distinct area (separately from the 15 bydeler), and leaving Oslo's own city centre off the map — exactly where many visitors book — would be a bigger gap than an inflated number with this caveat attached. This is Wandroz's official-data layer for Oslo — real Oslo kommune Statistikkbanken figures, not a qualitative or press-based judgment — and the source data is not split here by time of day, so both figures shown here are the same.

Frequently asked questions

Is Sentrum safe?

Wandroz currently rates Sentrum in Oslo, Norway as an area where Wandroz's data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Oslo, Norway, based on Oslo kommune's Statistikkbanken 2024 reported-offence figures. This source has no time-of-day breakdown, so this is one overall level rather than a separately measured day and night figure — see the note on this page before treating the day/night badges as independently measured.

Does Sentrum's rating cover night-time safety specifically?

Not separately. Oslo kommune's Statistikkbanken 2024 reported-offence figures publishes one figure per zone with no time-of-day split, so Sentrum's day and night badges show the same underlying level rather than an independently measured night figure. Treat it as a general indicator, not a night-specific measurement.

Is Sentrum a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Sentrum's rating is a useful general indicator, but this data is normalised against registered residents, not visitor footfall — busy tourist, transit or shopping areas can read higher without that meaning elevated risk for a visitor passing through. You can search accommodation already filtered to this specific area using the Booking.com link on this page.

What official data is Sentrum's rating based on?

Oslo kommune's Statistikkbanken 2024 reported-offence figures, covering Sentrum's real administrative boundary. This is a genuine official dataset, not a qualitative judgment or press research — see the methodology page for the exact figures, the year they cover, and how the rate is calculated.
